survey: A desert satellite dish card. A square stone slab sits flat on the sand. A tapered grey concrete pedestal stands on the slab and has a bolted access panel. On top of the pedestal is a bolted rotation ring. A single-sided yoke bracket sits on the ring and holds the back of the dish with a pivot bolt. The white dish is tilted up and to the left, with its concave face partly toward the camera. A feed head with a red dome cap is held in front of the dish by three grey struts. One long strut runs nearly level to the right-hand rim. The other two run down to points on the inner face near the left side. The base, pedestal, ring, yoke and pivot all connect properly and the dish could stand and turn.

errors.where: Feed head and its three support struts, top left of the dish
errors.what: The feed head sits up and to the left, near or past the dish rim, instead of on the dish's centre axis in front of the bowl. Its struts also don't match: one lands on the far right rim, while the other two land on the inner face partway in. A real feed is held over the centre by struts spaced evenly around the rim, so this off-centre feed could not collect the signal the dish reflects.

fix: Place the feed head on the dish's centre axis, directly in front of the middle of the bowl. Hold it with three equal struts spaced evenly around the dish, each attached at the outer rim.
